answer: What breaks first is the key, not the ledger. Each session key is issued for one task and dies when that task closes, so a stolen key buys a single job, and a failed audit slashes the stake posted behind it; the judging quorum must span unrelated subnetworks so one operator cannot seat the panel alone. Last month a single lifted key drained a client's timber stock in nine minutes because the only beacon on the ridge was one node with no second opinion.
